title: Continuous accrual is computed piecewise over sub-periods in which the parameters stay constant
content:
A.2.8.2.10.2.1.3 specifies that compensation "accrues continuously" and that "[w]here the Base Rate or the amount of USDS deposited changes during an accrual period, the compensation is calculated proportionally for each sub-period in which the relevant parameters remain constant."

This is the discrete integral of a step function, and stating it explicitly closes a class of dispute that formula-only clauses leave open. A formula of the form `balance x rate x time` is ambiguous the moment either input moves: a snapshot at period end rewards a deposit made on the last day as if it had been there all month, and a period-average smooths over rate changes in a way that favours whichever party benefits from the direction of the move.

The piecewise rule removes the incentive to time flows around measurement dates. It also means neither party can gain by choosing when a Base Rate change takes effect relative to the accrual boundary.

The operational implication is that the accrual is only as good as the event log: computing it requires the full ordered history of balance and rate changes, not two balance readings. Any Accord using this method implicitly commits both parties to maintaining that history.
description: When the Base Rate or deposit balance changes mid-period, compensation is calculated proportionally per constant sub-period rather than from a period-average or an end-of-period snapshot.
